examples.en: This year we're going to the book fair.
At the New Year's fair we drink mulled wine.

related.en: fair, exhibition (trade) — business: buying and selling, presentations, forums
fair (funfair) — for fun: cotton candy, carousels, souvenirs

note:
Typical combinations:
• са́јам књи̏га - book fair, сајам аутомобила - car show
• новогодишњи вашар - New Year's fair

examples.en: Where are you traveling from?
Where did you get the money?

related.en: where from (cause, source) — colloquial, with a touch of surprise
where from (from which place) — neutral, about a place

note: О̀ткуд is common in short questions: о̀ткуд зна̑ш? - «how do you know?», о̀ткуд ти о́вде? - «what are you doing here?»

examples.en: Give me a piece of the cake.
We bought three items of clothing.

related.en: piece, item — an object as a unit: «комад сапуна»
piece, slice — a cut-off part of a whole: «парче торте», «парче пице»

note: Ко̀ма̄д also means «a stage play»: позоришни комад. The rule is not strict.

examples.en: She opened a jar of ajvar.
Open a can of beans.
I drank a can of Coke.

related.en: glass jar — «тегла ајвара», «тегла џема»
tin can (food) — «конзерва пасуља»
aluminum can (drinks) — «лименка пива», «лименка кока-коле»

note: A bottle is фла̏ша or бо̏ца.

examples.en: Let's get out of the sun, into the shade.
His shadow could be seen on the wall.

related.en: shade — a cool spot out of the sun: «у хладу»
shadow (silhouette) — the dark image of an object on a surface

note: Се̑нка is also used figuratively: сенка сумње - «a shadow of doubt».

examples.en: My uncle on my mother's side lives in Belgrade.
My uncle on my father's side brought me a present.
The man at the kiosk sells newspapers.

related.en: uncle (mother's brother)
uncle (father's brother)
uncle, mister — not a relative, a way to address an adult man

note:
Uncles and aunts by marriage:
• wife of ујак - у̏јна
• wife of стриц - стри̑на
• husband of an aunt - те́так or те̏ча

examples.en: Think it over carefully before you decide.
I'll think about it.
I came up with a nickname for the dog.
Who invented the telephone?
They devised a new advertising campaign.
Just imagine we were millionaires!

related.en: to think over, think through — weigh something in advance
to think, ponder
to come up with — find an idea
to make up, invent; to lie
to devise, work out — think through in detail
to imagine, picture

note: One more verb of this family: предо̀мислити се - to change one's mind.

examples.en: Which juice do you want?
What is this juice like?

related.en: which — a choice among several
what kind of, what ... like — the quality of a thing

note: Ка̀ка̄в is also used in exclamations: ка̀ка̄в да̑н! - «what a day!»

meanings: пријатељ, друг, познаник, ортак or бураз?

examples.en: He's my best friend.
A friend of mine gave me this book.
He's just an acquaintance.
Buddy, come over for coffee!
Hey, bro, where have you been?

related.en: friend, close friend — a long-standing, close person
friend, pal (друг m., другарица f.) — a good acquaintance who may become a пријатељ
acquaintance
buddy, partner — colloquial: a mate or a friend
bro, buddy — an informal way to address a friend

note: A group of friends is дру́штво or еки́па. To become friends is спријатѐљити се.

meanings: зато, зато што, јер or пошто?

examples.en: It's late, so I'm going home.
I'm not going because I'm sick.
I'm going home because it's late.

examples.sr: [Збо̏г то́га што̏] је падала киша, утакмица је отказана.
examples.en: Because it was raining, the match was canceled.
Since it's late, I'm going home.

related.en: so, that's why — the result after the cause
because — the cause after the result
because, for — neutral, with a hint of «since»
because of the fact that — more formal
since, as — the cause stands at the beginning of the sentence

note: Trap: по̏што in a question means «how much»: по̏што је си̏р? - «how much is the cheese?»

examples.en: We like to talk over coffee.
We like to chat over coffee.
Don't babble so much.
The bishop addressed the faithful.

related.en: to tell, talk — neutral, everyday
to chat — a pleasant unhurried conversation
to babble, chatter — a lot and without much meaning, colloquial
to give a talk, address — bookish, solemn, rare

note:
Related words:
• бѐседа - a formal speech, sermon
• брбљѝвац - chatterbox

key: cmp:зајебавам се-зезам се-спрдам се-шалим се / шајем се

examples.en: I'm joking, don't be angry.
I'm just kidding.

examples.sr: Не [спр̏дај] се с њим, осетљив је.
examples.en: Don't make fun of him, he's sensitive.
Are you kidding me?

related.en: to joke — standard, neutral
to kid, joke around — colloquial, friendly tone
to tease, mock — a bit rude
to mess around, kid — vulgar

note: Ша́ла - «a joke, a jest», ви̏ц - «a joke (a funny story)».

meanings: «Be quiet» in Serbian: ћути, утишај се, умукни

examples.en: Be quiet, please, I'm trying to study.
Kids, quiet down, the baby is sleeping.
Shut up, I didn't ask you!

related.en: to be silent — neutral, both a request and a statement
to quiet down, speak more quietly — about volume: noisy kids, a too-loud argument
to shut up — rude; not said to elders or people you barely know

note:
Утишати се asks to lower the noise, not to stop talking.

У̀мукнути easily causes a conflict; with «бре» it sounds even more aggressive.

examples.en: Someone badmouthed me to the boss.

examples.sr: Никад га нећеш [надго̀ворити], увек има последњу реч.
examples.en: You'll never outtalk him, he always has the last word.

examples.sr: Пријатељи су ме [наго̀ворили] да пробам рафтинг.
examples.en: My friends talked me into trying rafting.
We arranged a meeting for Monday.
I didn't know what to answer.

examples.sr: Тешко ми је да [изго̀ворим] ово име.
examples.en: It's hard for me to pronounce this name.
Nobody dared to talk back to the director.

examples.sr: [До̀говорили] смо се да почнемо у осам.
examples.en: We agreed to start at eight.

related.en: to badmouth, gossip — speak ill of a person behind their back
to outtalk — get the upper hand in an argument, speak more convincingly or longer
to talk into — persuade someone to do something
to arrange, agree on — a date, a price, a meeting
to answer — give an answer to a question
to pronounce — a word, a name
to object, talk back — make a remark
to agree, come to an agreement

note:
The prefix changes the meaning completely. Do not mix up нагово̀рити («to talk into», persuade) and угово̀рити («to arrange»).

Догово̀рити without «се» means to finish saying something.

examples.en: - Thanks! - You're welcome!
A glass of water, please.
- Masha! - Yes?
Here you are, your water.
Please, have a seat.

related.en: please; you're welcome; yes? / pardon? — in reply to thanks and to a call, to begin a request, to ask someone to repeat
here you are, please — when offering or inviting

note: Изволите is said by the one who offers; in a shop the customer replies: «са̏мо да по̀гледа̄м» («I'm just looking»).

examples.en: What did you eat for breakfast?
Lunch will be ready at two.
I'll take an apple for a snack.
Tonight we're having dinner at Grandma's.

related.en: breakfast — verb доручковати
lunch — verb ручати
snack, afternoon snack — an apple, a banana; the verb ужинати means «to have a snack»
dinner, supper — verb вечерати

note:
Main trap: у̏жина is not dinner but a light snack between lunch and dinner. Dinner is вѐчера.

Colloquial: кло́па - food, кло́пати - to chow down.

examples.en: Which letter is missing?
«Mama» is a word of four letters.
There is cool shade under the old beech.

related.en: letter — a written character
word — a unit of speech
beech (the tree)

note:
сло̏во means a letter and ре̑ч a word, while бу̏ква is a beech tree.

A handy phrase to remember: «Ма̏ма је ре̑ч од чѐтири сло̑ва̄».

examples.en: Mom does the laundry every week.
Dad is peeling potatoes for lunch.
She wipes the dust every day.
I have to scrub the bathtub.

related.en: to wash — dishes, hands, hair, laundry, windows, a car
to clean; to peel — an apartment, a room, shoes, vegetables
to wipe — dust, a floor, a table
to scrub — with effort

note:
Teeth are «washed»: пра̏ти зу̑бе (to brush one's teeth). Shoes are «cleaned»: чистити обућу.

To tidy up a room is спре́мати со̏бу.

meanings: чаша, бокал, шоља or кригла: which vessel?

examples.en: Bring me a glass of wine.
The waiter brought a jug of water.
I'll have another cup of coffee.
We ordered two mugs of beer.

related.en: glass (wine glass, tumbler, shot glass) — named after the drink: чаша вина, чаша воде, чаша ракије
jug, pitcher, carafe — for water, juice or wine on the table
cup, mug with a handle — tea, coffee
beer mug — beer

note: A glass of wine is ча̏ша вина, while бо̀ка̄л вина is a whole jug of wine.

examples.en: I'm making lunch for the guests.
What are you doing tonight?
She works as a secretary.

related.en: to make, create, cook — when something comes into being as a result
to do, work — be busy with something

note: Something comes into being - пра̏вити: coffee, lunch, cakes, noise, problems. An activity or a job - ра́дити: homework, work.

examples.en: I'll try to pass the exam.
I'll make an effort to come on time.

related.en: to try, attempt — the result is unclear
to make an effort, try hard — the stress is on the effort

note: Both are usually followed by «да» and the present tense: по̀кушати да, потру́дити се да.

examples.en: I bought two tickets to Belgrade.
A museum ticket costs five hundred dinars.

related.en: ticket — for transport and for events; also a map or a playing card
admission ticket — for a concert, a match, a museum

note: For transport only ка̑рта is used, for example повратна карта - a round-trip ticket. For a concert or a museum both ка̑рта and у̀лазница work.

examples.en: He is the only son in the family.
It's a unique opportunity!
The child has a room of his own.

related.en: only, sole — једини син «only son», једина си ми «you're all I have»
united, single; unique — јединствена држава «a united country»
separate; special — посебна соба «a separate room», посебне потребе «special needs»

note: Common mistake: for «only» use јѐдӣнӣ; једѝнствен is closer to «united» or «unique».

examples.en: - Would you like some coffee? - Yes, thank you.
- Would you like some coffee? - No, thank you.

related.en: thank you, yes — accepting an offer
thank you, no — a polite refusal, or thanks for something

note: This is the rule taught at school. In practice many people do not follow it, and the meaning is clear from the intonation.

examples.en: I have a dog at home.
I'm going for a walk with the dog.
Our doggy loves to play.
We have a puppy at home.

related.en: dog — an adult dog, m.
dog, puppy — n.
doggy — affectionate, f.
puppy — n.

note: Forms: па̏с, gen. пса̏; ку̏че, gen. кучета; ку́ца, acc. куцу. Па̀шче is a rare word.

examples.en: The film made a good impression.

examples.sr: Твоје мишљење има велики [у̏тица̄ј] на њега.
examples.en: Your opinion has a big influence on him.

related.en: impression; imprint — оставити утисак, стећи утисак «to make an impression, to get an impression»
influence — имати утицај на некога «to have an influence on someone»

note: They sound alike. У̀тисак is what stays in your mind, у̏тица̄ј is an effect on someone or something. У̏тица̄ј is followed by «на» with the accusative: утицај на одлуку.

examples.en: The kids dye eggs for Easter.
I'm afraid of dogs.

related.en: to paint, dye, color — eggs, hair
to be afraid — with the genitive

note: In the present tense the forms look alike: бојим - «I dye», бојим се - «I'm afraid». Only «се» tells them apart.

examples.en: What time does class start?
What time is it now?
I've been waiting for him for a whole hour.

related.en: class, lesson; moment; o'clock — in formal time-telling
clock, watch; hour — as a length of time

note: The time is usually asked with са̑т: колико је сати? («what time is it?»). Ча̏с in a precise time is formal: у 22 ча̏са и 15 мину́та.

examples.en: I didn't hear well.

examples.sr: Он само [ћу̀ти] и гледа кроз прозор.
examples.en: He just keeps quiet and looks out of the window.
Look after the child until I come back.

related.en: to hear — ништа не чујем «I can't hear anything»
to be silent
to keep, guard, look after — пас чува кућу «the dog guards the house»

note: They sound alike but mean different things. Easy to mix up: чуо - «heard» and чувао - «kept, looked after».

key: cmp:изути / изувати-обути / обувати-обући / облачити-скинути / скидати-ставити / стављати

examples.en: Put on a jacket, it's cold.
Put on your shoes, we're in a hurry.
Put on a hat, it's snowing.
Take off those wet socks.
Please take off your shoes at the entrance.

related.en: to put on clothes; to dress someone — a jacket, a sweater, a T-shirt
to put on shoes — shoes, sneakers, heels
to put on an accessory; to put, place — glasses, a hat, a ring, a watch, lipstick
to take off — clothes, glasses, a hat; to undress
to take off shoes

note: Clothes - обу́ћи, shoes - о̀бути, jewelry and headwear - ста̏вити. Any item can be taken off with ски̏нути, and shoes also with ѝзути.

examples.en: Joking aside!
Open your book to page thirty.

examples.sr: Он је [стра́нац], али добро говори српски.
examples.en: He's a foreigner, but he speaks Serbian well.
Clients are received from 12 to 2 p.m.
Serbia is a small country.

related.en: side; page; flank — са стране «from the side», на све стране «on all sides»
page — of a book, a website
foreigner; stranger
political party; client, visitor of an office
country, state; land, soil

note: A country is зѐмља, not стра́на: стра́на зѐмља - «a foreign country», страни језик - «a foreign language».

examples.en: She got a nice tan at the seaside.
Wow, you're so tanned!
You really got a tan at the seaside!

related.en: to get tanned — the neutral word
to get dark, get very tanned — colloquial
to get a tan (literally «to get color») — as a compliment

note: Поцр̀нети literally means «to turn black» and is colloquial. Добити боју is most often said after a vacation.

examples.en: He threw the ball over the fence.
Over the winter I put on a few kilos.
Insert the card into the ATM.
They kicked him out of the club.
Transfer the money to my account.
Drop me off at work, please.

related.en: to throw
to throw on; to put on (weight)
to put in, insert; to throw in
to throw out, kick out; to dispense (of an ATM)
to throw over; to transfer (money); to reproach
to throw away, reject; to give someone a lift

note:
The prefix gives the direction:
• на- - on top of something
• «у-» - inside
• из- - out
• пре- - across, to another place
• од- - away, aside

examples.en: The little boy lost his ball.
My boyfriend works at a bank.
That young man is a medical student.
That guy is my neighbor.

related.en: boy — up to adolescence
boy, guy; boyfriend — colloquial
young man — formal
guy, young man; boyfriend — colloquial

note: «Boyfriend» is де̏чко or мо̀мак, «girlfriend» is дѐво̄јка.

examples.en: My family lives in Niš.
The whole extended family comes to the slava.

related.en: family — parents and children, the close circle
relatives, extended family — grandparents, aunts, cousins

note: A family name (surname) is прѐзиме, not фамилија.

examples.en: My uncle on my father's side lives in Novi Sad.
My uncle on my mother's side is a doctor.

related.en: uncle on the father's side, father's brother
uncle on the mother's side, mother's brother

note: The wife of стриц is стри̑на, the wife of ујак is у̏јна.

examples.en: On Saturday there's a wedding ceremony at the church.
I was at a friend's wedding.
We're going to the best man's wedding.

related.en: wedding ceremony; marriage — church or civil
wedding — the celebration
wedding guests; wedding — идемо у сватове «we're going to a wedding»

note: Венча́ње is only the ceremony. The whole celebration is сва̀дба, and сва̑тови are also the guests on the groom's side.

meanings: брдо, брег, планина, стена or зид?

examples.en: We live at the foot of a hill.
The house stands on a hill.
We'll spend the summer in the mountains.

examples.sr: Пењачи су се попели уз стрму [сте̑ну].
examples.en: The climbers scaled a steep rock face.
We hung a picture on the wall.

related.en: hill, small mountain — a modest elevation; брдо ствари «a heap of things»
hill, rise — a low one
mountain — a big one, often forested
rock, cliff
wall — of a building, a fence

note: A wall is зи̑д, while сте́на is a rock. A shore is о̏бала; бре̑г is a hill, not a bank.

examples.en: What a disgrace!
Aren't you ashamed to lie?
I blushed with shame.
We made a complete fool of ourselves at the match.

related.en: disgrace, shame — verbs брукати, обрукати се
shame, disgrace — about an action
shame — the feeling; стидим се «I'm ashamed», стидљив «shy»
disgrace, scandal — colloquial; бламирати (се) «to embarrass (oneself)»

note: Срамо̀та is shame about an action, сти̑д is only the feeling. Бру̏ка and блама́жа are more colloquial.

key: cmp:згодно ми је-одговара ми-таман ми је

examples.en: The size doesn't suit me.
This dress fits me just right.

examples.sr: Да ли ти је [зго̀дно] у четири?
examples.en: Is four o'clock convenient for you?

related.en: it suits me — size, color, price, time
it fits me just right — only about size
it's convenient for me — in time and place

note: Зго̏дан said of a person means «good-looking»: згодна девојка. It is not said that way about a dress.

examples.en: We bought a kilo of plums at the market.
Grandpa drinks plum brandy after lunch.
The neighbor makes grape brandy.

examples.sr: Најбоља је [ви̏шњевача] коју прави моја тетка.
examples.en: The best is the cherry brandy my aunt makes.

related.en: plum — the fruit; sometimes the brandy too
plum brandy — the classic rakija made from plums
grape brandy — from «лоза» (vine)
cherry brandy

note: Rakija is often named after the fruit. Ка̀јсија (apricot), ду̏ња (quince), кру̏шка (pear) are both the fruit and the rakija: «попићемо кајсију» - we'll have some apricot rakija. Rakija from Williams pears is виљамовка.

examples.en: I love you.
Kiss me!
Okay, bye, kisses!

related.en: to love, like — a person, a thing, food
to kiss — љубити се means «to kiss each other»
kisses, I kiss you — a fond goodbye; not a declaration of love

note: Trap: «to love» is во̀лети, while љу́бити is first of all «to kiss».

examples.en: Next Wednesday we're going to the movies.
Last Friday I was in Niš.
Next week we're going to the seaside.
My future husband is from Niš.

related.en: previous, last
upcoming, next
next — the neutral word
future — about a distant or abstract future

note: A day of the week or a period goes into the genitive without a preposition: претходне среде, наредног петка.

examples.en: Poor mother of mine, she works all day.
That is a poor family.

related.en: pitiful, poor (unfortunate) — someone to be pitied; јадница «poor thing»
poor, low-income — about wealth

note: Only сиро̀машан is used about poverty. Јадна is easily understood as «she is in a bad way», not «she has no money».

examples.en: I paid property tax.
The bank received a payment order.
I read a good review of that book.
The traffic officer gave me a fine.

related.en: order, instruction; account — налог за плаћање «payment order», налог на сајту «account on a website»
tax — VAT, income tax
presentation, review — приказ књиге «a book review»
punishment, fine — новчана казна «a monetary fine»

note: Tax is по̀рез; на́лог is an order or an account. При́каз means a presentation or review, ка̏зна a punishment or fine.

examples.en: I did only one task.
I've done only one task so far.
I had just got home.
He's just about to leave.

related.en: only, just — and nothing more: a limitation, an exception
only, just; just now — so far only this stage has been reached
just now — about a recent event
about to, any moment now

note: Са̏мо јѐдан зада́так - one and nothing more. Те̏к јѐдан зада́так - only one so far, more to come.

key: cmp:недостајеш ми-ужелео сам те се-фалиш ми-чезнем за тобом

examples.en: I miss you so much.
I miss you.
How I've missed you!
I long for you every day.

related.en: I miss you, I'm missing you — neutral and the most common
I miss you — colloquial
I've missed you — after a long separation
I long for you — bookish, strong yearning

note: The sentence is built the other way round: the subject is the person who is missed. Недостајеш ми literally means «you are lacking to me».

examples.en: We bought a pumpkin for the soup.
Grandma wears a new fur coat.
Grandpa wears a fur hat when it's cold.

related.en: pumpkin — the vegetable
fur coat — warm winter outerwear
fur hat — a traditional headgear

note: They sound alike, so keep them apart: a fur coat is бу̑нда, while шу̀бара is a hat.

examples.en: He is good at doing math in his head.
The kids are counting apples.
I'm counting on him.

related.en: to calculate, do sums in your head; to count on — рачунати на некога «to count on someone»
to count objects, list — броји до десет «count to ten», наброј градове «name some cities»

note: Рачу̀нати comes from ра̀чӯн (account, calculation), бро̀јати from бро̑ј (number). Related words: рачу̀на̄р - computer, рачуново̀дство - accounting, бројаница - rosary.

examples.en: Thank you very much!
- Would you like some coffee? - Yes, thank you.
- Would you like some coffee? - No, thank you.
I'm grateful to you.

related.en: thanks — the basic word
thank you, yes — as a rule, accepting an offer
thank you, no — as a rule, a polite refusal
grateful — noun захвалност «gratitude»

note: You can strengthen хва́ла like this: хва́ла ле̑по, хвала најлепше, пу̏но хва́ла. Not everyone keeps the distinction between захваљујем and захваљујем се.

examples.en: This is my new car.
The wheel fell off the bicycle.

related.en: car — plural only, neuter: ова кола «this car»
wheel — a single one; pl. точкови

examples.en: He plays chess with his grandfather.
I like to dance at weddings.
The children are playing with a ball.
Today we're playing store.

related.en: to play (a game, a sport); to dance; to act (a role)
to dance — sounds less common than играти
to play, frolic — with a toy, in a children's game

note: Ѝграти without «се» is used for sports, cards, chess, a role, and also for a dance: ѝграти ко̏ло. With «се» it is children's games and fun: и̏гра̄мо се ра́та - we're playing war.

examples.sr: То је била само [ша́ла], не љути се.
examples.en: It was just a joke, don't be angry.
A real crush started in front of the stage.

examples.sr: Ово је био јак [шу̏т] ка голу.
examples.en: That was a strong shot at the goal.

related.en: joke — the ordinary word: без шале «no kidding», шалити се «to joke»
crush, shoving in front of the stage at a rock concert — slang
kick at the ball, shot — шутирати, шутнути «to shoot, to kick»

note: The ordinary word for a joke is ша́ла. Шу̏тка is a different word.

examples.en: Last night we talked for a long time.
Tonight we're going to Grandma's.
I didn't sleep well last night.

related.en: last night, yesterday evening
tonight, this evening
tonight, last night — the night just past or the one coming

note: The line between evening and night is fuzzy, and even Serbs struggle to say when но̀ћас is. It is simpler to use си̏но̄ћ for the past and вечѐрас for the future.

meanings: обићи, посетити, свратити or наћи се?

examples.sr: [О̀бишла] сам баку и донела јој лекове.
examples.en: I went to see Grandma and brought her medicine.
We'll visit you on Saturday.
Yesterday I dropped by Grandma's.

examples.sr: [На̏шла] сам се са баком у граду.
examples.en: I met Grandma in town.

related.en: to check in on, look in on — make sure everything is fine; to walk around
to visit, pay a visit — neutral or formal
to drop by — briefly, on the way, without a plan
to meet up — by arrangement

note: All four mean some kind of visiting or meeting, but they differ in the plan: свра́тити - no plan, на́ћи се - only by arrangement.

examples.sr: Ја сам гладна, [а] Игор је жедан.
examples.en: I'm hungry, and Igor is thirsty.
I didn't see it, I heard it.
She is taller than Svetlana.

related.en: and, but — contrast after a positive statement
but, rather — after a negative
than — in a comparison

note: After a negative use не̏го instead of «а»: нисам гладна, него уморна - «I'm not hungry, but tired». A memory aid: «минус, него плус».

key: cmp:не хоће да знају-неће да знају-неће знати
meanings: неће да знају or неће знати?

examples.en: He doesn't want to go to Moscow.
They won't know the answer.
I don't want to know anything about it.

related.en: they don't want to know — refusal, unwillingness
they won't know — future, negative
a mistake — not said this way in Serbian

note: The negative of хте̏ти is written as one word: не́ћу, неће. «Doesn't want to do» takes неће да with the present tense, while неће with an infinitive means «will not do».

examples.en: We put the shelf in the corner of the room.
I buy cigarettes at the kiosk on the corner.
We made a play corner.

related.en: corner, angle — neutral, also in geometry
corner — a Turkish loanword, colloquial
cozy corner, nook

note: Ћо̀шак is most often the corner of a street or room in everyday speech. Ку́так is less common, usually with a purpose: ку́так за и̏гру - a play corner.

examples.en: We're flying to Rome via Frankfurt.
The technician ran the cable through the hallway.

related.en: across, over; via an intermediate point
through — inside something

note: Different cases follow: пре̏ко takes the genitive, кроз the accusative.

examples.en: I have to wash the floor.
Mom is scrubbing the bathtub.
Every morning she wipes the dust off the shelves.
Every morning I mop the hall.

related.en: to wash — the general verb: a floor, dishes
to scrub — thoroughly, with a brush or cloth
to wipe — with a damp or dry cloth
to mop — colloquial; also «to jog»

note: Nearby: усиса́вати - to vacuum, метлати - to sweep a yard or garage.
